Its original form is "al-mutazammil," and the ta' was assimilated into the zay, making it heavy. Anyone who wraps himself in his garment has "tazammal." Al-Zajjaj said: "It was assimilated into it because of their proximity." The exegetes said: The Prophet ﷺ used to wrap himself in his garments at the beginning of what came to him from Jibril, out of fear of him, until he became familiar with him. Al-Suddi said: He had wrapped himself for sleep. Muqatil said: He had come out of the house having put on his garments, and Jibril called to him: "O you who are wrapped." It was said: What is meant is "one wrapped in prophethood." 'Ikrimah said regarding the meaning of this verse: "You have been wrapped in this matter, so stand up to it." It was also said: The reason he was not addressed here as "the Prophet" or "the Messenger" is that he had not yet delivered (the message); he was then only at the beginning of revelation.

A man would not know how much he had prayed or how much of the night remained, so he would stand the whole night out of fear that he would not preserve the required amount. Then this was abrogated (naskh) for him and for them by His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand (in prayer) less than two-thirds of the night...﴾ up to the end of the verse. This is the view of a group of exegetes, and they said: There is no surah in the Qur'an whose last part abrogated its first part except this surah. It was also said: It was abrogated for the community, but its obligation remained upon him forever. It was also said: It was obligatory upon him alone, not upon them. One: a year. Ibn 'Abbas said: Between the beginning of "al-Muzzammil" and its end was a year.

The second: sixteen months, related by al-Mawardi.

His saying, ﴿And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation﴾: we have already mentioned tartil (measured recitation) in [al-Furqan 32].

His saying, ﴿Indeed, We will bestow upon you a heavy word﴾: this is the Qur'an. Regarding the meaning of its heaviness there are six views.

The second: that acting upon it is heavy because of its obligations and rulings. This was said by al-Hasan and Qatadah.

The third: that it will be heavy in the scale on the Day of Resurrection. This was said by Ibn Zayd.

The fourth: that it is majestic, as one says of a sensible man: "He is dignified and weighty." This was said by 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Yahya.

The fifth: that it is neither light nor trivial, because it is the speech of the Lord, Mighty and Majestic. This was said by al-Farra'.

The sixth: that it is a word that has weight in its soundness, its clarity, and its benefit, as you say: "This is a sound speech, and this is a weighty word when you test it." This was mentioned by al-Zajjaj.

The second: that it is standing (in prayer) after sleep. This is the saying of 'A'ishah and Ibn al-A'rabi, and Ahmad explicitly stated it in the narration of al-Marwadhi.

The third: that it is what comes after 'Isha'. This was said by al-Hasan, Mujahid, Qatadah, and Abu Mijlaz.

The fourth: that it is the beginning of the night. This was said by 'Ata' and 'Ikrimah.

The fifth: that it is standing (in prayer) at the end of the night. This was said by Yaman and Ibn Kaysan.

From this is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "O Allah, make Your tread harsh upon Mudar." Ibn Qutaybah mentioned the meaning of both readings. Ibn Muhaysin read "ashaddu wita'an" with a fatha on the waw and the ta', and with a long vowel.

It is said: "I carded the cotton" (sabbakhtu al-qutn), meaning I fluffed it. The meaning of "fluffed" is "spread out," so the meaning would be: Indeed, for you by day there is extensive spreading out.

His saying, ﴿And mention the name of your Lord﴾: that is, during the day as well. ﴿And devote yourself to Him with complete devotion﴾: Mujahid said: "Be sincere to Him with sincerity." Ibn Qutaybah said: "Cut yourself off to Him," from your saying "I cut the thing" (battaltu al-shay') when you severed it. Al-Zajjaj said: "Cut yourself off to Him in worship." The second: that they are the sons of al-Mughirah ibn 'Abd Allah. This was said by Muqatil ibn Sulayman.

The third: that they are the mockers, who are the chieftains of Quraysh, related by al-Tha'labi.

One: that it is a thorn that catches in the throat, so that it neither goes in nor comes out. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas and 'Ikrimah. The second: zaqqum. This was said by Muqatil. The third: al-dari'. This was said by al-Zajjaj.

The fourth: zaqqum, ghislin, and al-dari', related by al-Tha'labi.

His saying, ﴿On the Day the earth quakes﴾: al-Zajjaj said: It is in the accusative (manṣūb) by the saying ﴿Indeed, with Us are shackles﴾. His saying, ﴿And the mountains will be...﴾: Muqatil said: The meaning is: they will become, after their hardness and strength, ﴿sand heaped up﴾. Al-Farra' said: "Kathib" is sand. Al-Zajjaj said: Its plural of "kathib" is "kuthban," which are large pieces of sand. "Mahil" means flowing.

His saying, ﴿Indeed, We have sent to you﴾: that is, the people of Makkah ﴿a messenger﴾: that is, Muhammad ﷺ, [p. 393] ﴿as a witness over you﴾ regarding the delivery (of the message), and the faith of those who believed and the disbelief of those who disbelieved, ﴿just as We sent to Pharaoh a messenger﴾: he is Musa, peace be upon him. "Wabil" means severe. Ibn Qutaybah said: It is from your saying: "I found the place unwholesome" (istawbaltu al-makan), when you found it unhealthy. It is said: "kala' mustawbal," meaning pasture that is not wholesome. Al-Zajjaj said: "Wabil" means heavy and extremely harsh. From it a great rain is called "wabil." Muqatil said: The intended meaning of this "wabil" seizure is drowning. This is a warning to the disbelievers of Makkah that punishment may descend upon them for their denial, just as it descended upon Pharaoh.

His saying, ﴿Then how will you protect yourselves, if you disbelieve, from a Day﴾: that is, from the punishment of a day. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: By what means will you shield yourselves from the punishment of a day whose terror makes the child grey-haired without (the cause of) old age? Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Abu 'Imran read "naj'alu al-wildan" (نَجْعَلُ الوِلْدانَ) with a nun.

His saying, ﴿The sky will be split by it﴾: al-Farra' said: "al-sama'" (the sky) may be treated as masculine or feminine. Here it is used in the masculine sense. A poet said:

"If the sky were to raise a people up to Him, we would be lifted up with the sky along with the clouds."

Al-Zajjaj said: The masculinization of "al-sama'" is of two kinds. One: that the meaning of "al-sama'" is the meaning of "the ceiling." The second: according to their saying "murdi'" (a nursing woman) in the manner of attribution. The meaning is: "the sky is one having splitting," just as the nursing woman is one having nursing. Ibn Qutaybah said: The meaning of the verse is: "The sky is split by it," that is, in it, meaning on that day.

(p-395) His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, His promise is ever fulfilled﴾. That is because it is a promise of the Resurrection, so it will certainly come to pass without doubt.

Its original form is "al-mutazammil," and the ta' was assimilated into the zay, making it heavy. Anyone who wraps himself in his garment has "tazammal." Al-Zajjaj said: "It was assimilated into it because of their proximity." The exegetes said: The Prophet ﷺ used to wrap himself in his garments at the beginning of what came to him from Jibril, out of fear of him, until he became familiar with him. Al-Suddi said: He had wrapped himself for sleep. Muqatil said: He had come out of the house having put on his garments, and Jibril called to him: "O you who are wrapped." It was said: What is meant is "one wrapped in prophethood." 'Ikrimah said regarding the meaning of this verse: "You have been wrapped in this matter, so stand up to it." It was also said: The reason he was not addressed here as "the Prophet" or "the Messenger" is that he had not yet delivered (the message); he was then only at the beginning of revelation.

A man would not know how much he had prayed or how much of the night remained, so he would stand the whole night out of fear that he would not preserve the required amount. Then this was abrogated (naskh) for him and for them by His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand (in prayer) less than two-thirds of the night...﴾ up to the end of the verse. This is the view of a group of exegetes, and they said: There is no surah in the Qur'an whose last part abrogated its first part except this surah. It was also said: It was abrogated for the community, but its obligation remained upon him forever. It was also said: It was obligatory upon him alone, not upon them. One: a year. Ibn 'Abbas said: Between the beginning of "al-Muzzammil" and its end was a year.

The second: sixteen months, related by al-Mawardi.

His saying, ﴿And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation﴾: we have already mentioned tartil (measured recitation) in [al-Furqan 32].

His saying, ﴿Indeed, We will bestow upon you a heavy word﴾: this is the Qur'an. Regarding the meaning of its heaviness there are six views.

The second: that acting upon it is heavy because of its obligations and rulings. This was said by al-Hasan and Qatadah.

The third: that it will be heavy in the scale on the Day of Resurrection. This was said by Ibn Zayd.

The fourth: that it is majestic, as one says of a sensible man: "He is dignified and weighty." This was said by 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Yahya.

The fifth: that it is neither light nor trivial, because it is the speech of the Lord, Mighty and Majestic. This was said by al-Farra'.

The sixth: that it is a word that has weight in its soundness, its clarity, and its benefit, as you say: "This is a sound speech, and this is a weighty word when you test it." This was mentioned by al-Zajjaj.

The second: that it is standing (in prayer) after sleep. This is the saying of 'A'ishah and Ibn al-A'rabi, and Ahmad explicitly stated it in the narration of al-Marwadhi.

The third: that it is what comes after 'Isha'. This was said by al-Hasan, Mujahid, Qatadah, and Abu Mijlaz.

The fourth: that it is the beginning of the night. This was said by 'Ata' and 'Ikrimah.

The fifth: that it is standing (in prayer) at the end of the night. This was said by Yaman and Ibn Kaysan.

From this is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "O Allah, make Your tread harsh upon Mudar." Ibn Qutaybah mentioned the meaning of both readings. Ibn Muhaysin read "ashaddu wita'an" with a fatha on the waw and the ta', and with a long vowel.

It is said: "I carded the cotton" (sabbakhtu al-qutn), meaning I fluffed it. The meaning of "fluffed" is "spread out," so the meaning would be: Indeed, for you by day there is extensive spreading out.

His saying, ﴿And mention the name of your Lord﴾: that is, during the day as well. ﴿And devote yourself to Him with complete devotion﴾: Mujahid said: "Be sincere to Him with sincerity." Ibn Qutaybah said: "Cut yourself off to Him," from your saying "I cut the thing" (battaltu al-shay') when you severed it. Al-Zajjaj said: "Cut yourself off to Him in worship." The second: that they are the sons of al-Mughirah ibn 'Abd Allah. This was said by Muqatil ibn Sulayman.

The third: that they are the mockers, who are the chieftains of Quraysh, related by al-Tha'labi.

One: that it is a thorn that catches in the throat, so that it neither goes in nor comes out. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas and 'Ikrimah. The second: zaqqum. This was said by Muqatil. The third: al-dari'. This was said by al-Zajjaj.

The fourth: zaqqum, ghislin, and al-dari', related by al-Tha'labi.

His saying, ﴿On the Day the earth quakes﴾: al-Zajjaj said: It is in the accusative (manṣūb) by the saying ﴿Indeed, with Us are shackles﴾. His saying, ﴿And the mountains will be...﴾: Muqatil said: The meaning is: they will become, after their hardness and strength, ﴿sand heaped up﴾. Al-Farra' said: "Kathib" is sand. Al-Zajjaj said: Its plural of "kathib" is "kuthban," which are large pieces of sand. "Mahil" means flowing.

His saying, ﴿Indeed, We have sent to you﴾: that is, the people of Makkah ﴿a messenger﴾: that is, Muhammad ﷺ, [p. 393] ﴿as a witness over you﴾ regarding the delivery (of the message), and the faith of those who believed and the disbelief of those who disbelieved, ﴿just as We sent to Pharaoh a messenger﴾: he is Musa, peace be upon him. "Wabil" means severe. Ibn Qutaybah said: It is from your saying: "I found the place unwholesome" (istawbaltu al-makan), when you found it unhealthy. It is said: "kala' mustawbal," meaning pasture that is not wholesome. Al-Zajjaj said: "Wabil" means heavy and extremely harsh. From it a great rain is called "wabil." Muqatil said: The intended meaning of this "wabil" seizure is drowning. This is a warning to the disbelievers of Makkah that punishment may descend upon them for their denial, just as it descended upon Pharaoh.

His saying, ﴿Then how will you protect yourselves, if you disbelieve, from a Day﴾: that is, from the punishment of a day. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: By what means will you shield yourselves from the punishment of a day whose terror makes the child grey-haired without (the cause of) old age? Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Abu 'Imran read "naj'alu al-wildan" (نَجْعَلُ الوِلْدانَ) with a nun.

His saying, ﴿The sky will be split by it﴾: al-Farra' said: "al-sama'" (the sky) may be treated as masculine or feminine. Here it is used in the masculine sense. A poet said:

"If the sky were to raise a people up to Him, we would be lifted up with the sky along with the clouds."

Al-Zajjaj said: The masculinization of "al-sama'" is of two kinds. One: that the meaning of "al-sama'" is the meaning of "the ceiling." The second: according to their saying "murdi'" (a nursing woman) in the manner of attribution. The meaning is: "the sky is one having splitting," just as the nursing woman is one having nursing. Ibn Qutaybah said: The meaning of the verse is: "The sky is split by it," that is, in it, meaning on that day.

(p-395) His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, His promise is ever fulfilled﴾. That is because it is a promise of the Resurrection, so it will certainly come to pass without doubt.

Its original form is "al-mutazammil," and the ta' was assimilated into the zay, making it heavy. Anyone who wraps himself in his garment has "tazammal." Al-Zajjaj said: "It was assimilated into it because of their proximity." The exegetes said: The Prophet ﷺ used to wrap himself in his garments at the beginning of what came to him from Jibril, out of fear of him, until he became familiar with him. Al-Suddi said: He had wrapped himself for sleep. Muqatil said: He had come out of the house having put on his garments, and Jibril called to him: "O you who are wrapped." It was said: What is meant is "one wrapped in prophethood." 'Ikrimah said regarding the meaning of this verse: "You have been wrapped in this matter, so stand up to it." It was also said: The reason he was not addressed here as "the Prophet" or "the Messenger" is that he had not yet delivered (the message); he was then only at the beginning of revelation.

A man would not know how much he had prayed or how much of the night remained, so he would stand the whole night out of fear that he would not preserve the required amount. Then this was abrogated (naskh) for him and for them by His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand (in prayer) less than two-thirds of the night...﴾ up to the end of the verse. This is the view of a group of exegetes, and they said: There is no surah in the Qur'an whose last part abrogated its first part except this surah. It was also said: It was abrogated for the community, but its obligation remained upon him forever. It was also said: It was obligatory upon him alone, not upon them. One: a year. Ibn 'Abbas said: Between the beginning of "al-Muzzammil" and its end was a year.

The second: sixteen months, related by al-Mawardi.

His saying, ﴿And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation﴾: we have already mentioned tartil (measured recitation) in [al-Furqan 32].

His saying, ﴿Indeed, We will bestow upon you a heavy word﴾: this is the Qur'an. Regarding the meaning of its heaviness there are six views.

The second: that acting upon it is heavy because of its obligations and rulings. This was said by al-Hasan and Qatadah.

The third: that it will be heavy in the scale on the Day of Resurrection. This was said by Ibn Zayd.

The fourth: that it is majestic, as one says of a sensible man: "He is dignified and weighty." This was said by 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Yahya.

The fifth: that it is neither light nor trivial, because it is the speech of the Lord, Mighty and Majestic. This was said by al-Farra'.

The sixth: that it is a word that has weight in its soundness, its clarity, and its benefit, as you say: "This is a sound speech, and this is a weighty word when you test it." This was mentioned by al-Zajjaj.

The second: that it is standing (in prayer) after sleep. This is the saying of 'A'ishah and Ibn al-A'rabi, and Ahmad explicitly stated it in the narration of al-Marwadhi.

The third: that it is what comes after 'Isha'. This was said by al-Hasan, Mujahid, Qatadah, and Abu Mijlaz.

The fourth: that it is the beginning of the night. This was said by 'Ata' and 'Ikrimah.

The fifth: that it is standing (in prayer) at the end of the night. This was said by Yaman and Ibn Kaysan.

From this is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "O Allah, make Your tread harsh upon Mudar." Ibn Qutaybah mentioned the meaning of both readings. Ibn Muhaysin read "ashaddu wita'an" with a fatha on the waw and the ta', and with a long vowel.

It is said: "I carded the cotton" (sabbakhtu al-qutn), meaning I fluffed it. The meaning of "fluffed" is "spread out," so the meaning would be: Indeed, for you by day there is extensive spreading out.

His saying, ﴿And mention the name of your Lord﴾: that is, during the day as well. ﴿And devote yourself to Him with complete devotion﴾: Mujahid said: "Be sincere to Him with sincerity." Ibn Qutaybah said: "Cut yourself off to Him," from your saying "I cut the thing" (battaltu al-shay') when you severed it. Al-Zajjaj said: "Cut yourself off to Him in worship." The second: that they are the sons of al-Mughirah ibn 'Abd Allah. This was said by Muqatil ibn Sulayman.

The third: that they are the mockers, who are the chieftains of Quraysh, related by al-Tha'labi.

One: that it is a thorn that catches in the throat, so that it neither goes in nor comes out. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas and 'Ikrimah. The second: zaqqum. This was said by Muqatil. The third: al-dari'. This was said by al-Zajjaj.

The fourth: zaqqum, ghislin, and al-dari', related by al-Tha'labi.

His saying, ﴿On the Day the earth quakes﴾: al-Zajjaj said: It is in the accusative (manṣūb) by the saying ﴿Indeed, with Us are shackles﴾. His saying, ﴿And the mountains will be...﴾: Muqatil said: The meaning is: they will become, after their hardness and strength, ﴿sand heaped up﴾. Al-Farra' said: "Kathib" is sand. Al-Zajjaj said: Its plural of "kathib" is "kuthban," which are large pieces of sand. "Mahil" means flowing.

His saying, ﴿Indeed, We have sent to you﴾: that is, the people of Makkah ﴿a messenger﴾: that is, Muhammad ﷺ, [p. 393] ﴿as a witness over you﴾ regarding the delivery (of the message), and the faith of those who believed and the disbelief of those who disbelieved, ﴿just as We sent to Pharaoh a messenger﴾: he is Musa, peace be upon him. "Wabil" means severe. Ibn Qutaybah said: It is from your saying: "I found the place unwholesome" (istawbaltu al-makan), when you found it unhealthy. It is said: "kala' mustawbal," meaning pasture that is not wholesome. Al-Zajjaj said: "Wabil" means heavy and extremely harsh. From it a great rain is called "wabil." Muqatil said: The intended meaning of this "wabil" seizure is drowning. This is a warning to the disbelievers of Makkah that punishment may descend upon them for their denial, just as it descended upon Pharaoh.

His saying, ﴿Then how will you protect yourselves, if you disbelieve, from a Day﴾: that is, from the punishment of a day. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: By what means will you shield yourselves from the punishment of a day whose terror makes the child grey-haired without (the cause of) old age? Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Abu 'Imran read "naj'alu al-wildan" (نَجْعَلُ الوِلْدانَ) with a nun.

His saying, ﴿The sky will be split by it﴾: al-Farra' said: "al-sama'" (the sky) may be treated as masculine or feminine. Here it is used in the masculine sense. A poet said:

"If the sky were to raise a people up to Him, we would be lifted up with the sky along with the clouds."

Al-Zajjaj said: The masculinization of "al-sama'" is of two kinds. One: that the meaning of "al-sama'" is the meaning of "the ceiling." The second: according to their saying "murdi'" (a nursing woman) in the manner of attribution. The meaning is: "the sky is one having splitting," just as the nursing woman is one having nursing. Ibn Qutaybah said: The meaning of the verse is: "The sky is split by it," that is, in it, meaning on that day.

(p-395) His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, His promise is ever fulfilled﴾. That is because it is a promise of the Resurrection, so it will certainly come to pass without doubt.

It is the verbal noun of "wataita fulanan 'ala kadha, muwata'atan wa wita'an" (I agreed with someone upon such a thing). They intended that in the recitation at night, the heart, tongue, and hearing of the one praying agree together in understanding the Qur'an and mastering its interpretation. From this is His saying: ﴿so that they may agree upon the number of what Allah has forbidden﴾ [al-Tawbah 37]. The rest read "wat'an" (وَطْأً) with a fatha on the waw and without a long vowel. The meaning is: it is heavier upon the one praying than the hours of the day. From the speech of the Arabs: "The tread (wat'ah) of the ruler became harsh upon the people," when what is required of them becomes burdensome. From this is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "O Allah, make Your tread harsh upon Mudar." Ibn Qutaybah mentioned the meaning of both readings. Ibn Muhaysin read "ashaddu wita'an" with a fatha on the waw and the ta', and with a long vowel.

[p. 392]

His saying, ﴿And more upright in speech﴾: that is, more sincere for speech and more audible to it, because during the night voices are still, so the recitation becomes pure, the heart is free to understand the recitation, and there is no barrier between it and his hearing and understanding.

His saying, ﴿Indeed, for you by day is extensive occupation﴾: that is, free time for your sleep and rest. So make the rising of the night for your worship. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas and 'Ata'. 'Ali, Ibn Mas'ud, Abu 'Imran, and Ibn Abi 'Ablah read "sabakhan" (سَبَخًا) with the letter kha' (خ). Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning in the language is sound. It is said: "I carded the cotton" (sabbakhtu al-qutn), meaning I fluffed it. The meaning of "fluffed" is "spread out," so the meaning would be: Indeed, for you by day there is extensive spreading out.

His saying, ﴿And mention the name of your Lord﴾: that is, during the day as well. ﴿And devote yourself to Him with complete devotion﴾: Mujahid said: "Be sincere to Him with sincerity." Ibn Qutaybah said: "Cut yourself off to Him," from your saying "I cut the thing" (battaltu al-shay') when you severed it. Al-Zajjaj said: "Cut yourself off to Him in worship." From this Mary is called "al-batul," because she devoted herself to Allah, the Exalted, in worship. Likewise a "batlah" charity is one cut off from the property of the giver. The basic form of the verbal noun of "tabattala" is "tabattul," but the Exalted saying ﴿tabtil﴾ is understood as the meaning of "tabattal."

His saying, ﴿Lord of the east...﴾: Ibn Kathir, Nafi', Abu 'Amr, and Hafs from 'Asim read "Rabbu" with a damma (رَبُّ). Ibn 'Amir, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Abu Bakr from 'Asim read it with a kasra (رَبِّ). What follows this has already been discussed [al-Shu'ara' 28], up to His saying: ﴿And be patient over what they say﴾ of denial against you and harm, ﴿and part from them with gracious parting﴾ without any impatience in it. This verse is, according to the exegetes, abrogated by the verse of the sword. ﴿And leave Me with the deniers﴾: that is, do not concern yourself with them, for I will suffice you against them. ﴿The people of luxury﴾: meaning those given to comfort. Regarding who is meant by this there are three views.

One: that they are the food-givers at Badr. This was said by Muqatil ibn Hayyan.

The second: that they are the sons of al-Mughirah ibn 'Abd Allah. This was said by Muqatil ibn Sulayman.

The third: that they are the mockers, who are the chieftains of Quraysh, related by al-Tha'labi.

His saying, ﴿And give them respite a little﴾: 'A'ishah said: "It was not but a short time until the battle of Badr occurred." Some exegetes held that this verse is abrogated by the verse of the sword, but this is not correct.

His saying, ﴿Indeed, with Us are shackles﴾: these are the fetters, the singular of which is "nakl." We have already explained the meaning of "al-Jahim" in [al-Baqarah 119]. ﴿And food that chokes﴾: this is that which cannot be swallowed down the throat. Regarding it the exegetes have four views.

One: that it is a thorn that catches in the throat, so that it neither goes in nor comes out. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas and 'Ikrimah. The second: zaqqum. This was said by Muqatil. The third: al-dari'. This was said by al-Zajjaj.

The fourth: zaqqum, ghislin, and al-dari', related by al-Tha'labi.

His saying, ﴿On the Day the earth quakes﴾: al-Zajjaj said: It is in the accusative (manṣūb) by the saying ﴿Indeed, with Us are shackles﴾. The meaning is: He will punish the disbelievers and torment them ﴿on the Day the earth quakes﴾, that is, it will be shaken and moved with the most violent movement.

His saying, ﴿And the mountains will be...﴾: Muqatil said: The meaning is: they will become, after their hardness and strength, ﴿sand heaped up﴾. Al-Farra' said: "Kathib" is sand. "Mahil" is that whose base has moved, so that it collapses on you from above. The Arabs say "mahil" and "mahyul," and "makil" and "makyul." Al-Zajjaj said: Its plural of "kathib" is "kuthban," which are large pieces of sand. "Mahil" means flowing.

His saying, ﴿Indeed, We have sent to you﴾: that is, the people of Makkah ﴿a messenger﴾: that is, Muhammad ﷺ, [p. 393] ﴿as a witness over you﴾ regarding the delivery (of the message), and the faith of those who believed and the disbelief of those who disbelieved, ﴿just as We sent to Pharaoh a messenger﴾: he is Musa, peace be upon him. "Wabil" means severe. Ibn Qutaybah said: It is from your saying: "I found the place unwholesome" (istawbaltu al-makan), when you found it unhealthy. It is said: "kala' mustawbal," meaning pasture that is not wholesome. Al-Zajjaj said: "Wabil" means heavy and extremely harsh. From it a great rain is called "wabil." Muqatil said: The intended meaning of this "wabil" seizure is drowning. This is a warning to the disbelievers of Makkah that punishment may descend upon them for their denial, just as it descended upon Pharaoh.

His saying, ﴿Then how will you protect yourselves, if you disbelieve, from a Day﴾: that is, from the punishment of a day. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: By what means will you shield yourselves from the punishment of a day whose terror makes the child grey-haired without (the cause of) old age? Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Abu 'Imran read "naj'alu al-wildan" (نَجْعَلُ الوِلْدانَ) with a nun.

His saying, ﴿The sky will be split by it﴾: al-Farra' said: "al-sama'" (the sky) may be treated as masculine or feminine. Here it is used in the masculine sense. A poet said:

"If the sky were to raise a people up to Him, we would be lifted up with the sky along with the clouds."

Al-Zajjaj said: The masculinization of "al-sama'" is of two kinds. One: that the meaning of "al-sama'" is the meaning of "the ceiling." The second: according to their saying "murdi'" (a nursing woman) in the manner of attribution. The meaning is: "the sky is one having splitting," just as the nursing woman is one having nursing. Ibn Qutaybah said: The meaning of the verse is: "The sky is split by it," that is, in it, meaning on that day.

(p-395) His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, His promise is ever fulfilled﴾. That is because it is a promise of the Resurrection, so it will certainly come to pass without doubt.

"Verily this" — i.e., the verses of the Qur'an — "is a reminder" — i.e., an admonition and an exhortation — "so whoever wills may take a path to his Lord" — through faith and obedience.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] less than two-thirds of the night, or half of it, or a third of it﴾ — i.e., less. Ibn Kathir and the people of Kufa read "adna" and "thuluthahu" with a fatha on the fa' and the tha', while the rest read them with a kasra on both.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and a group of those with you [also do so]﴾ — meaning the believers. ﴿And Allah determines the night and the day﴾ — He knows their measures, so He knows the amount of the night in which you stand [in prayer]. ﴿He knew that you would not be able to keep count of it﴾ — and concerning this there are two views.

One: you will not be able to sustain standing two-thirds of the night, nor a third of the night, nor half the night; this is the view of Muqatil. The second: you will not be able to observe the exact times of the night; this is the view of al-Farra'. ﴿So He turned to you [in forgiveness]﴾ — i.e., He returned to you with forgiveness and lightening [of the obligation]. ﴿So recite what is easy for you﴾ — upon you — ﴿of the Qur'an﴾ — meaning in prayer, without fixing a specific time. Al-Hasan said: it is what is recited in the Maghrib and 'Isha' prayers.

Then He mentioned their excuses, saying: ﴿He knows that there will be among you those who are ill﴾, so they cannot sustain the night prayer; ﴿and others travelling through the land seeking of Allah's bounty﴾ — these are those who travel for trade — seeking of His provision, so they cannot sustain the night prayer; ﴿and others fighting in the way of Allah﴾ — these are the fighters in jihad, so they cannot sustain the night prayer. ﴿So recite what is easy of the Qur'an﴾.

It is mentioned that this ruling was abrogated for the Muslims by the five daily prayers, and this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And establish prayer﴾ — i.e., the five prayers at their appointed times — ﴿and give zakah and loan Allah a good loan﴾. Its explanation has already preceded [al-Hadid: 18]. Ibn 'Abbas said: he means other than zakah, in maintaining ties of kinship and hosting guests. ﴿And whatever good you put forward for yourselves, you will find it with Allah﴾ — i.e., you will find its reward in the Hereafter. ﴿It is better and greater in reward﴾. Abu 'Ubayda said: the meaning is "you will find it better." Al-Zajjaj said: "huwa" has entered as a separator (fasl). The commentators said: the meaning of "better" is: more excellent than what you have given, ﴿and greater in reward﴾ than what you delay until the time of bequest at death.
